introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Information and Communication Technologies 2 (0796), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You will be marked on your ability to use good English to organize information clearly and to use specialist vocabulary where appropriate. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Explain TWO impacts of computer virus to a school information system. (2 marks)

(b) Give TWO ways to protect computers in a school from virus attack. (2 marks)

(c) State two computer health related problems and give a measure to prevent each. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Two impacts of a computer virus on a school information system (2 marks)**

- **Loss or corruption of data**: a virus can delete, modify or encrypt files such as student records, marks and timetables, so the school loses important information if there is no backup.
- **Disruption and slowing down of the system**: the virus uses the memory and the processor, so the computers become slow or crash, and it can spread through the school network and flash drives to all the computers, so teaching and administration are interrupted and the cost of cleaning and restoring the system is high.
- (Other valid answers: confidential data may be stolen; the school may have to replace damaged hardware or software.)

**(b) Two ways to protect the computers (2 marks)**

- Install a good **antivirus program** and keep its virus definitions **updated**; scan the computers and every flash drive regularly.
- **Do not open e-mail attachments or download files from unknown sources**; keep the operating system patched, use a firewall, and keep regular **backups**.

**(c) Two computer health problems and a preventive measure for each (2 marks)**

| Health problem | Preventive measure |
|---|---|
| Repetitive strain injury (RSI) of the wrists and fingers caused by long typing or mouse use | Take regular breaks, use a wrist rest and an ergonomic keyboard and mouse. |
| Eye strain and headaches caused by looking at the screen for long periods | Use an anti-glare screen, adjust the brightness and the room lighting, and look away from the screen regularly (for example every 20 minutes). |

(Another valid problem is back and neck pain; the measure is an adjustable chair with back support and a correct sitting posture.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Briefly explain relational database model. (2 marks)

(b) Explain THREE disadvantages of a database management system. (3 marks)

(c) A school intends to create a student record database, state and explain TWO rules from the Data Protection Act you would advise the school to comply with. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) The relational database model (2 marks)**

In the relational model the data are organised in **tables (relations)**. Each table is made of **rows (records or tuples)**, one per entity, and **columns (fields or attributes)**. Each table has a **primary key** that identifies each row uniquely, and the tables are **linked by foreign keys** (for example a `class_id` field in the STUDENT table that matches the primary key of the CLASS table), so that every fact is stored only once and the data can be combined with queries (SQL).

**(b) Three disadvantages of a DBMS (3 marks)**

- **High cost**: the DBMS software, the more powerful hardware and the training of the staff (and of a database administrator) are expensive.
- **Complexity**: the design, installation and management of a DBMS need specialised skills; a bad design gives poor performance.
- **Vulnerability (single point of failure)**: all the data are in a central place, so if the DBMS or the server fails, or if the data are lost or attacked, all the users and applications are affected; strong backup and security procedures are needed.

**(c) Two rules of the Data Protection Act (2 marks)**

- Data must be **accurate and kept up to date**: the school must correct wrong details (names, addresses, marks) and update the records, because wrong data can harm the students.
- Data must be **kept secure** and used **only for the purpose for which they were collected**: the school must use passwords and access rights so that only authorised staff see the records, and must not give the data to other people (for example advertisers) without permission.
- (Other valid rules: data must be obtained and processed fairly and lawfully; data must not be kept longer than necessary; the data collected must be adequate, relevant and not excessive; people have the right to see the data held about them.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of each of the following printers:

(a) Laser printer. (2 marks)

(b) Inkjet printer. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Printer | One advantage | One disadvantage |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) Laser printer** (2 marks) | It prints **quickly** with **high quality** and is cheap per page for large print jobs; it is quiet. | It is **expensive to buy** (especially colour models) and the toner cartridges are expensive; it is bulky and heavy. |
| **(b) Inkjet printer** (2 marks) | It is **cheap to buy**, small, and gives very good **colour** pictures and photographs. | It is **slow** and the **ink cartridges are expensive** for the number of pages printed; the ink can smudge on wet paper and the nozzles can clog. |
